summary: Kalyan Kumar Sarkar was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. Her academic posts at Stony Brook University include director (attested 2007) and Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a historian of Buddhism who studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg. She also held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at Cornell from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from Charles University in 1952. He worked at the Oriental Institute (1952–1970) and was a professor of Dravidian studies at Utrecht University (~1976–1992).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (b. 1934) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya. He has served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor to the IGNCA (attested 2009).

Kammie Morrison Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned her PhD from the University of Virginia in 2009 under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune (~1964–1968), later lecturing at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982).
Kanchu Onoe is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and served as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Calgary, studying under MA supervisor A. W. Barber (attested 1999) as well as Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.
Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris. He later held an appointment at the Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has taught at Rissho University, serving as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under the traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (both attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu universities. She founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, serving as its trustee, Academic Director, and chairperson.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (b. 1955) is an Indian historian and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman in 1989 and became a professor at the University of Delhi in 1995.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate from Palacký University. He taught Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990) and later served as a professor at Masaryk University (1993–1998).

Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg (PhD 1983) and has held a long-term professorship at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2026).
Karen Katsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and held a post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
